emma_research: Quick note from an onboarding run of ember32k-int3 on dedicated: intermittent token slips around long numeric and citation spans when using fine-grain prefill + index-squeeze. Short repro below.
fred_infra: Flags? image tag? which cluster?
emma_research: serve: `./serve --model ember32k-int3 --prefill=fine-grain --prefill-granularity=8 --kv=index-squeeze --quant=int3_var --compress-meta=true` image: gh/onboard/ember-int3:run-54 cluster: ded-7
gina_eval: sample (fp16 vs int3):
```
FP16: "In the 2024 report, Section 4.2 cites the original dataset from Dr. Alvarez."
INT3: "In the 2024 report Section 4.2 cites original dataset Dr. Alvarez."
```
henry_platform: Looks like punctuation drops and occasional token reorder at long citation windows. Any kv checksums / index maps?
emma_research: kv-checksum outputs: fp16=0x4c9a11e2, int3(squeeze)=0x8b7e00f4, int3(no-squeeze)=0x4c9a11e2. ran `rope-phase-delta --fp fp16 --quant int3 --window 15000` -> max delta 0.0027 rad at pos 14288.
fred_infra: That strongly implicates the index-squeeze path. Hypothesis: squeeze remaps slots but RoPE multipliers are computed before remap. Can you run `export DEBUG_ROPE_REMAP=1` and paste the short log around pos 14272..14304?
emma_research: pasted excerpt: `pre-remap-pos=14280 mult=0.9932 -> remapped-slot=14279` (shows off-by-one remap at tile boundary).\
gina_eval: goldset (7 anchors) perp: fp16=7.6 int3(squeeze)=11.2 int3(no-squeeze)=7.8. So squeeze path regresses.
henry_platform: Mitigation: disable index-squeeze for canary and open a PR to compute RoPE after remapping. Also add a unit test: tiny synthetic kv with granularity>1 assert multipliers match baseline after remap. ci-bot: build 19777: gh/onboard/ember-int3:run-54 pushed to staging :white_check_mark:\
emma_research: I'll rerun with squeeze disabled, deterministic seed, and post rope diffs + updated goldset numbers here. If fixed, I'll open PR titled "fix(kv): compute RoPE multipliers after index-squeeze remap (granularity>1)" and include unit test.
fred_infra: Nice. If canary fails, prioritize revert. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
